newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Daewoo Motor says to resume car exports to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo Motor says to resume car exports to U.S.

text.p: Daewoo Motor Co Ltd, an affiliate of South Korea's Daewoo Group, said on Tuesday it would resume car exports to the U.S. in late 1997 or early 1998.
"We plan to tap the U.S. market again late this year or early next year," said Kim Seung-il, a Daewoo Motor spokesman.
He said Daewoo planned to export 30,000 cars to the world's largest car market in 1998, and 100,000 units in 2000.
Daewoo had agreed to stay out of the U.S. market through 1995 when it ended its partnership with General Motors Corp in late 1992.
Kim said Daewoo would set up direct sales outlets in four areas of the U.S.
Models scheduled for export to the U.S. include the Lanos and Nubira compact cars and the Leganza mid-sized sedan, he said.
Daewoo began marketing the Lanos domestically from November 1996, the Nubira from February and the Leganza from April.
The company also said it would export those three models to other countries in the second half of this year.
"Those new models will be exported to 60 countries around the world by February 1998," Kim of Daewoo said.

Daewoo launched development of the models in 1993 after its divorce with GM. During their 15-year partnership, Daewoo and the American car giant were frequently at odds over sales strategy, investment decisions and Daewoo's plans to sell its cars independently in some overseas markets.
Daewoo Motor, which earned 23 billion won in net profits in 1996 on sales of 4.3 trillion won, plans to increase the profit to 70 billion won this year on sales of 6.8 trillion won.
Kim said Daewoo planned to sell 885,000 vehicles this year, of which 400,000 units were for export.
In 1996, Daewoo Motor's vehicle sales totalled 653,098 units, of which 352,916 were exported, he said.
